title: Number of Islands
description: Given an m x n 2D binary grid which represents a map of '1's (land) and '0's (water), return the number of islands. An island is surrounded by water and is formed by connecting adjacent lands horizontally or vertically. You may assume all four edges of the grid are all surrounded by water.
constraints: Land cells connect horizontally or vertically, not diagonally
The grid is provided as an array of strings, each representing a row

examples.explanation: All the connected land cells form a single island.
There are three separate groups of connected land cells, forming three islands.

title: Course Schedule
description: There are a total of numCourses courses you have to take, labeled from 0 to numCourses - 1. You are given an array prerequisites where prerequisites[i] = [ai, bi] indicates that you must take course bi first if you want to take course ai. Return true if you can finish all courses, otherwise return false. This requires detecting whether the prerequisite graph contains a cycle.
constraints: 0 <= ai, bi < numCourses, and all pairs are unique

examples.explanation: There are 2 courses, and to take course 1 you must first take course 0. This is possible.
To take course 1 you need course 0, and to take course 0 you need course 1, forming a cycle.

title: Clone Graph Node Count
description: Given an undirected connected graph represented by an adjacency list adjList, where adjList[i] is a list of node values that node i+1 (1-indexed) is connected to, determine the total number of nodes reachable from node 1, including node 1 itself. This simulates verifying a graph clone would contain the correct number of nodes.
constraints: Each node's neighbors are given as a list of 1-indexed node values
The graph is undirected and connected from node 1's perspective
No self-loops or duplicate edges exist in adjList

examples.explanation: Starting from node 1, all 4 nodes are reachable through the connections given.
There is only one node with no neighbors, so only 1 node is reachable.

title: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix
description: Given an n x n binary matrix grid, return the length of the shortest clear path in the matrix. If there is no clear path, return -1. A clear path is a path from the top-left cell (0,0) to the bottom-right cell (n-1,n-1) such that all visited cells are 0, and all adjacent cells in the path are 8-directionally connected (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally). The length of a clear path is the number of visited cells.
constraints: Movement is allowed in all 8 directions

examples.explanation: The path goes from (0,0) diagonally to (1,1), giving a path length of 2.
The shortest clear path visits 4 cells to reach the bottom-right corner.

title: Network Delay Time
description: You are given a network of n nodes, labeled from 1 to n. You are also given times, a list of travel times as directed edges times[i] = (ui, vi, wi), where ui is the source node, vi is the target node, and wi is the time it takes for a signal to travel from source to target. We will send a signal from a given node k. Return the minimum time it takes for all the n nodes to receive the signal. If it is impossible for all the n nodes to receive the signal, return -1.
constraints: 1 <= ui, vi, k <= n, and 0 <= wi <= 100

examples.explanation: It takes 2 units of time for the signal to reach all nodes starting from node 2.
It takes 1 unit of time to reach node 2 from node 1.
